region_chill_delivered_provenance.pnw: pnw (2026-07-14, maritime Pacific Northwest region arc, Task 3, zones 8-9) reconciled to WSU Skagit County Extension / WSU Mount Vernon NWREC: Skagit Valley AWN (Agricultural Weather Network) station data, 2007-2015, banks 968 to 1950 chill hours annually (average ~1468) -- Hunter, 'The Importance of Chilling,' WSU Skagit County Extension, 2016. Model: Utah / modified-Weinberger chill hours, accumulated hours with temperature between 32 and 45 degrees F over the winter dormant season (the model already carried in this table's definition); note the WSU Skagit source itself flags that its own station figure uses a simpler 'hour below 45 degF' proxy rather than the strict 32-45 degF window, a close but not identical match in a maritime winter that rarely sustains long stretches below 32 degF. pnw z8 (Puget Sound / Willamette Valley lowlands, e.g. Skagit Valley / Mount Vernon WA, the WSU NWREC station site) is the direct station-sourced band: [968, 1950]. pnw z9 (milder coastal / protected pockets, e.g. immediate WA/OR coast) has no distinct T1 station chill figure located in this pass; [700, 1500] is a reasoned, deliberately conservative-lower-bounded estimate from the same 32-45 degF model and the same general maritime winter regime -- milder coastal minimum temperatures (per the zone's own extreme-minimum-temperature definition) do not necessarily mean less time spent in the 32-45 degF chill window, since maritime marine-layer winters characteristically linger in that cool damp band rather than swinging to hard freeze or above-45 degF warmth. This z9 band is an ESTIMATE, not a station-sourced figure, and should be tightened with a direct coastal-station chill record (e.g. an OSU Aurora/Willamette Valley or immediate-coast Oregon/Washington station) before it backs a z9-specific per-variety chill-required certification claim. Both bands clear the ~600-1000 hour fruiting threshold comfortably and sit far above rgv's near-frost-free [0,300] floor, consistent with the maritime PNW's well-documented reputation among temperate tree-fruit and small-fruit growers for reliable, ample winter chill (unlike se_gulf [650,1000] or ca_interior [500,1100] at the same zone-8 label -- the maritime PNW's long, mild, damp winters bank more chill than either despite sharing a zone number, because continental/subtropical climates swing through the 32-45 degF band quickly rather than lingering in it). z8's low bound (968) exceeds z9's low bound (700), matching the convention used elsewhere in this table that the colder-lowland-winter zone carries the higher chill floor. Per-variety chill-REQUIRED (chill_hours_required / chill_hours_range) is the separate axis and is unchanged by this addition.
